answer: A verifiable delay function plus hardware attestation blocks Sybils: each new identity must finish a sequential delay computation before joining, and no zephyr of extra cores can shorten it, so a farm pays real wall-clock time per fake. The identity must also present a device attestation proving it runs on distinct hardware, and the vertex of trust is that one machine can hold only a few identities, so bulk Sybils need bulk hardware. The cipher sealing the attestation keeps honest onboarding cheap: one short delay and one check, while an attacker pays minutes and a hardware bill per clone.
